description:
NARROWED 2026-09-05 — MY ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS TOO STRONG AND IS CORRECTED BELOW. The residual defect is real but smaller than filed.

THE RESIDUAL, TRUE CLAIM. The compose TRACE records `semantic_reason` (400 chars) for a semantic rejection but carries no equivalent for an apply failure — only `apply_failed: true` and `ops_applied: <count>` (development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, trace metadata around lines 6185-6200). So a query over traces can say THAT an apply failed but not WHY, and apply-failure classes cannot be aggregated on the trace surface the learning loop reads. The reason exists at that point: the per-op result type at feature-compose.ts:4525 is `{ path, kind, ok, repaired?, detail?, span? }`, and the full array WITH detail is written to the compose report at line 6139 under PROPOSALS_DIR (default /workspace/proposals).

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I originally wrote that the detail is 'recoverable only by knowing the gap id and reading a file inside the container, which no automated consumer does'. THAT IS FALSE. An automated consumer does read it. My failed dispatch produced the gap `recommit-route-edit-f06d9ed8-anchor_not_found`, whose summary reads: 'compose for gap route-edit-f06d9ed8 repeated already-recorded failure class anchor_not_found: {"error":"no_unique_anchor: refused fs_edit — planned anchor is non-unique and re-derivation found no unique substring (would mislocalize to first occurrence)"}'. So the reason is captured verbatim AND assigned a named failure class (anchor_not_found), AND recognised as REPEATED — the recommit path is tracking recurrence of apply-failure classes. The gap's classification_metadata also carries a failure_lessons array with {at, class, reason, raw_excerpt}. The system is doing more of this than I credited.

SO THE DEFECT IS NARROWER: attribution exists in the GAP store and is class-labelled there; it is absent from the TRACE. That still matters, because the trace is the aggregatable surface the learning loop and audits read, and because only gaps that go through the recommit path get the treatment — an apply failure on a dispatch with no gap lineage leaves nothing. But 'apply failures are unattributed' as a blanket statement is wrong.

THE UNDERLYING BEHAVIOUR WAS CORRECT. The applier detected that the planned anchor was ambiguous, refused rather than mislocalizing to the first occurrence, and rolled back cleanly (ops_applied 0, rolled_back true, no partial state). That is the anchor-relocation failure mode being PREVENTED. The fault in that dispatch was mine: I quoted a NON-UNIQUE line as context in the goal and the drafter anchored on it. Rule learned and worth keeping: never quote a non-unique line in a goal, even as context; anchor by replacing a line unique by construction, and name the line that must NOT be used.

FALSIFIER (unchanged in form): query traces for template_id=feature_compose with metadata.apply_failed=true and group by failure reason. That grouping is impossible today. After a fix every apply_failed trace must carry a non-empty reason and the grouped count must equal the count of apply_failed traces. NOTE when re-checking: the gap store already answers this question for the subset with recommit lineage, so a fix here is about the trace surface and about coverage of dispatches without a gap, not about creating the information.
